newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard scolds aborigines on Olympic boycott call.
newsitem.headline: Howard scolds aborigines on Olympic boycott call.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, dogged by widespread criticism for his solution to a native land rights row, on Wednesday scolded Aborigines for urging a boycott of the 2000 Sydney olympics.
"I say to the Aboriginal people with the best will in the world, stop talking like that," Howard said.
"Every time they open their mouths and they talk like that, they lose further support within mainstream Australia.
"No Australian ... wants to see this country hurt, wants to see this country humiliated, wants to see the farm product of this country denigrated or boycotted."
Howard said in a radio interview his compromise was a fair solution that protected Aborigines and farmers.

But one Aboriginal group, protesting Howard's planned compromise, on Tuesday repeated earlier threats to lobby black nations to boycott the Olympic Games and said it may consider a consumer boycott of Australian exports.
But an Aboriginal leader on Wednesday said a boycott was not being considered by the main Aboriginal group negotiating over land rights.
"Our...working party is not talking about those things at the present time," Charles Perkins said in a radio interview.
